# Where 20CLIPS Works | Short-Form Video Editing
URL: https://20clips.com/locations/

Home / Locations 
 Short-form video editing for the UAE, the UK and Australia
 20CLIPS is a remote video editing service: 20 ready-to-publish short-form videos every month for a flat $999. Choose your country.
 Book a Call 
 See pricing 
 One service, three country pages and six city pages
 20CLIPS has no offices to visit and no studio to book. It is a remote editing service: you upload raw footage to a shared folder, and finished vertical videos come back for review. That is why the service, the price and the way it works are the same everywhere, and why the pages below answer the questions that matter in each place instead of describing different offers.
 Each country page lists all seven services available there, with a cost guide, a hiring guide and an examples page for every one. The city pages add local context for the sectors that use the service most. If you would rather start from finished work, the catalogue groups real edits by niche and the work page shows everything in one grid.
 Choose your country
 The UAE
 Businesses and creators in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, from property and hospitality to clinics and personal brands. Start at the UAE hub , or go straight to Dubai or Abu Dhabi .
 The UK
 Brands, agencies and creators in London, Manchester and beyond, from e-commerce to professional services. Start at the UK hub , or go to London or Manchester .
 Australia
 Owner-operators, coaches, venues and online stores in Sydney, Melbourne and regional areas. Start at the Australia hub , or go to Sydney or Melbourne .
 What's included
 Every plan includes the same complete monthly system.
 Reels, TikTok & YouTube Shorts formatting
 Captions & subtitles on every video
 B-roll & visual enhancements
 Sound design & music
 Basic motion graphics
 Hook & pacing optimization
 9:16 vertical delivery
 2 revisions per video

 What stays the same wherever you are
 The price is $999 a month in US dollars for 20 videos, roughly $50 each, with captions, b-roll, sound design and music, basic motion graphics, hook and pacing optimization and 9:16 delivery in every video. The pricing does not differ by country, and the full list is on the pricing page .
 Turnaround and your delivery schedule are set on a 30-minute onboarding call, based on your volume, so nobody is working to an assumption.
 In every country
 20 short-form videos a month
 A flat $999, in US dollars
 2 revisions per video
 Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts formatting
 No long-term commitment
 A shared folder for footage
 How remote editing fits different working patterns
 A business in the Gulf may film in the evening and review the next morning. A team in the UK may upload straight after a shoot day. An owner in a regional Australian town may film between jobs and review edits once the day is done. A shared folder and a review step suit all three, because nobody has to be in the same room or even awake at the same time.
 The same logic applies to creators. Whether you record a podcast in a spare room or a studio, you send the recording and the clips return. For ideas on how many videos suit your channel, read how many short-form videos to post each week .
 Services you can use in every country
 Seven services sit inside the monthly package: short-form video editing , Instagram Reels editing , TikTok editing , YouTube Shorts editing , UGC video editing , podcast clip editing and the monthly package . Each has a worldwide overview and a page for every country.
 The service is also built for creators , brands and agencies , and paid creative work is covered by performance creative editing .
 FAQ
 Where does 20CLIPS work?
 20CLIPS is a remote service that works with clients worldwide. Choose your country on this page to see how it works for you.
 Is the price different by country?
 No. It is $999 a month for 20 short-form videos, in US dollars, with no per-video fees and no long-term commitment.
 Is there anywhere I need to visit?
 No. Everything is done online through a shared folder, so there is nothing to visit.
 How do I get started?
 Book a 30-minute call. Footage goes into a shared folder, and your edited videos come back for review, with 2 revisions per video.
 Which country page should I read?
 Read the one for the country you operate in. They cover the same services with local examples and answers.
 Can I use the service from another country?
 Yes. It is remote, so it works from anywhere. The country pages are guides, not limits.
 Can I see examples before I decide?
 Yes. The catalogue groups finished edits by niche, and the work page shows the full set.
 Do you post the videos?
 No. You receive finished files to publish yourself.
 You already have the footage. Now turn it into content.

 Why browse by niche
 Most people who look at editing work are really asking one question: has this studio edited something like mine? A grid of unrelated clips cannot answer that, so the catalogue groups the portfolio by what the videos are about, from cars and real estate to podcasts and food. Each niche page shows the videos, describes what is in each one and explains what makes that kind of edit work.
 Every niche page also points to the services and country pages behind it, so you can go from an example to the price, the process and a call in a couple of clicks.
 Work by niche

 The seven services behind the work
 The examples come from the same monthly package. Short-form video editing covers the general service, Reels editing and TikTok editing focus on a platform, YouTube Shorts editing cuts from long videos, UGC editing works with creator footage, podcast clip editing works with episodes and the monthly package ties it together.
 Each service has a page for every country: the UAE , the UK and Australia . The price is $999 a month for 20 videos, whichever you choose, and the pricing page lists what is included.
 How to use the catalogue
 Start with the niche closest to your own content and watch the videos. Then read the short notes under each one: they say what the edit is doing, such as opening on a detail, framing a speaker or cutting to a beat, so you can decide whether that approach suits you.
 When something fits, follow the links from the niche page to the matching service and country page, where the price, the process and the answers to common questions are laid out. If nothing fits exactly, describe your footage on the 30-minute call and the editor will say how it would be handled.
 Where the service runs
 Editing is remote, so the cities below are guides, not boundaries: Dubai , Abu Dhabi , London , Manchester , Sydney and Melbourne . The locations page explains how the same service fits each country.
 If you want to see everything in one place, the work page shows the full portfolio grid.

 They are edits from the 20CLIPS portfolio. Each niche page describes what is in every video.

 Yes. Send raw footage and references and ask for a similar style at onboarding.

 The package suits any footage that works as short-form video. Describe it on the 30-minute call.

# Short-Form Video Editing Service | 20CLIPS
URL: https://20clips.com/short-form-video-editing/

Home / Short-Form Video Editing 
 Short-Form Video Editing Service
 20CLIPS turns raw footage into polished short-form videos for Instagram Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts: 20 ready-to-publish videos every month.
 Book a Call 
 See examples 
 Examples
 A sample of relevant edits. See more on the work page .
 Vox Pop Street interview: relationships 
 &times; 
 What is short-form video editing?
 Short-form video is now the main way audiences discover creators and brands, but posting consistently is difficult when editing 20+ vertical videos a month sits on top of everything else you do. 20CLIPS handles the editing every month for a flat $999.
 Every video is built around the same fundamentals: a hook that earns attention in the first two seconds, pacing that holds it through the middle, and a clean cut that leaves people wanting the next one. We handle captions, b-roll, sound design and basic motion graphics on every edit, formatted for Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts.
 Who it's for
 Content creators publishing daily or weekly across platforms
 Founders and personal brands turning ideas into content
 Podcasters who want episodes repurposed into Shorts
 DTC and e-commerce brands with product or UGC footage
 Marketing teams and agencies that need reliable monthly output
 What's included
 Every plan includes the same complete monthly system.
 Reels, TikTok & YouTube Shorts formatting
 Captions & subtitles on every video
 B-roll & visual enhancements
 Sound design & music
 Basic motion graphics
 Hook & pacing optimization
 9:16 vertical delivery
 2 revisions per video
 This covers
 Hooks: the first two seconds are cut and re-cut until the video earns a watch-through
 Pacing: cuts, zooms and pattern interrupts keep retention high
 Captions: burned-in captions and subtitles for silent viewing
 B-roll: supporting footage and cutaways where useful
 Sound design: music, effects and clean audio levels
 Motion graphics: basic titles, callouts and transitions
 Platform formatting: correct aspect ratio and specs per platform

 You send footage on a rolling basis and get a predictable stream of ready-to-publish videos back, edited to a consistent standard across Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts.

 FAQ
 What counts as "footage" I can send you?
 Raw camera footage, phone recordings, podcast recordings, screen recordings, UGC clips, or existing long-form video you want repurposed. If you're not sure it will work, ask on a call.
 Do you write scripts or hooks from scratch?
 We edit and optimize the footage you provide, including trimming and reordering for stronger hooks and pacing. We don't write scripts or produce original footage.
 Can I request specific styles or reference videos?
 Yes. Most clients share reference videos and brand guidelines during onboarding, and we match that style consistently across all 20 videos.
 What if I don't need all 20 videos in a given month?
 Unused videos don't roll over, but most clients send footage in batches and use the full 20 each month once their workflow is set up.

 What is Instagram Reels video editing?
 Instagram Reels rewards fast hooks, clean pacing and native-feeling edits. 20CLIPS is a dedicated Reels video editing service: send raw clips and get back polished, on-brand Reels: 20 a month, for $999.
 Whether you're filming talking-head content, repurposing a podcast, or working from UGC and product footage, every Reel is edited with Instagram's format and audience behavior in mind: vertical framing, safe zones for captions and UI, and pacing built for a feed where the average viewer decides in under two seconds.

 Do you edit Reels for Instagram specifically, or is it the same as TikTok editing?
 The offer covers Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts together: most footage gets edited into versions for all three platforms as part of your 20 monthly videos.

 FAQ
 What makes TikTok editing different from Reels or Shorts?
 The core edit is similar, but pacing, caption placement and hook style are adjusted for TikTok's native feel and audience expectations.
 Can you edit both organic and paid TikTok content?

 Yes, most clients send footage in smaller batches throughout the month rather than one large drop.

 What is podcast video editing?
 A single podcast episode usually contains several strong short-form moments. 20CLIPS turns your long-form podcast recordings into polished, ready-to-publish Reels, TikToks and YouTube Shorts: 20 videos a month for $999.

# Short-form video editing service in the UAE | 20CLIPS

Home / Locations / Video editing in the UAE / Short-form video editing 
 Short-form video editing service for the UAE
 A short-form video editing service for businesses and creators in the UAE: send raw footage, get 20 captioned, ready-to-publish vertical videos back every month for a flat $999.
 Book a Call 
 See pricing 
 What a short-form video editing service does for a UAE business
 Most UAE businesses already own more footage than they can use. A property developer has site walkthroughs on a phone, a restaurant group has service footage from every opening night, a clinic has doctors explaining treatments, and a founder has an hour of talking recorded in a studio. Turning any of it into a vertical video that holds attention for thirty seconds is a separate job, and it is the job this service takes over.
 20CLIPS works from the footage you send. An editor finds the strongest moment, rebuilds the opening so the point lands first, cuts the pauses, adds captions that read with the sound off, brings in b-roll and music, and exports a 9:16 file formatted for Instagram Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts. You review each video, ask for changes, and publish. The service itself is the same everywhere; this page explains how it fits businesses in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and the rest of the country.
 The price is a single line: $999 a month, in US dollars, for 20 finished videos. That works out to roughly $50 per video, and nothing is added per video, so a UAE finance team can put one number in the budget and leave it there. The pricing page has the full list of what is included.
 Who uses it across the UAE
 The footage differs from sector to sector. The way it becomes a good short video does not.
 Property and development
 Show-flat tours, site progress, investor briefings and agent explainers all cut well into short clips. The edit opens on the view or the headline figure and keeps text minimal. See how YouTube Shorts editing can reuse the same briefings.
 Hospitality and restaurants
 Plating, pours, interiors and event nights are made for the format. A good edit shortens each shot to the moment of appeal and lets sound do the selling.
 Clinics, wellness and beauty
 Practitioners explaining a procedure or a routine on camera need the pauses taken out and the claims captioned clearly, so a viewer follows without sound.
 Retail, fashion and automotive
 Product features, lookbooks and showroom reels depend on movement, close-ups and clean colour, all handled in the edit.
 Founders, consultants and personal brands
 Talking-head content is the easiest to produce and the easiest to get wrong. Tight cutting and captions turn a monologue into something people finish. This guide for personal brands covers the approach.

 What good short-form editing looks like
 Five things you should be able to see in every finished video.
 The first second carries the point
 The opening shows the result, the surprising line or the question. Greetings and logo animations are cut. When footage is a long recording, the editor often moves the best sentence to the front.
 Pacing follows the speech
 Dead air goes, and the picture changes when the idea changes. A zoom, a cutaway or a caption highlight lands on the word that matters instead of on a fixed timer.
 Captions are part of the design
 They are accurate, large enough for a phone held at arm's length, timed to the speaker and kept clear of the buttons each platform draws on top of the video.
 Sound is finished, not left raw
 Voice levels are balanced, music sits under the speech and effects are used sparingly. Cheap audio loses a viewer faster than a plain picture.
 The look stays consistent
 Fonts, colours, caption style and transitions are agreed at onboarding from your references, then repeated across all 20 videos so the feed looks like one account.
 How a month works, step by step
 Everything starts with a 30-minute call. You describe what you film and where you publish, share a few reference videos and brand files, and agree how often footage will arrive. Turnaround and your delivery schedule are set on that call, based on your volume, rather than promised in advance.
 After that, footage goes into a shared folder whenever you have it. Most UAE clients send in batches: a shoot day in Dubai Marina on Tuesday, a recorded podcast on Thursday, a launch event at the weekend. Each batch is edited into videos that come back for review. Every video includes 2 revisions, so a changed caption or a different opening is a note, not a new order.
 Approved videos are finished files. Posting stays with you or your social team, as does anything that requires a decision about timing, so there is nothing to learn and no software to install. This explainer describes what an editor actually does in each step.
 What to send, and what to avoid sending
 The most useful habit is to send full recordings along with clips. A single long conversation recorded in a Downtown studio can supply several of your 20 videos, because the editor picks the self-contained moments instead of working with whatever you pre-selected.
 Raw camera or phone footage in the best quality you have
 Longer recordings, such as podcasts, webinars and talks, that hold several short moments
 Reference videos and your brand fonts, colours and logo
 Timestamps for any line that must be included
 Licensed music only if you want a specific track
 Mistakes that cost a revision
 Footage already compressed by a social app, which lowers quality
 Only the highlights, leaving no choice of opening
 Changing the brand look every week
 Briefing five people separately instead of sending combined notes
 Waiting until the last week of the month to send everything
 Freelancer, in-house editor or a monthly package
 UAE companies usually weigh three routes. A freelancer is flexible, but briefing starts again with every job and quality depends on who is free that week. An in-house editor gives you someone embedded in the business, with visa, salary, equipment and management time attached, which pays off only when there is constant video work well beyond 20 a month.
 A monthly package sits between them. The price and the process stay the same each month, the style is matched to your references, and you can cancel anytime because there is no long-term commitment. The detail is on what short-form editing costs in the UAE and how to hire short-form editing in the UAE .
 A sample month for a UAE account
 An illustration of the rhythm, not a forecast of views or followers.
 Week one
 Book the call, share references and send the first shoot: a showroom, a menu launch or a founder recording. Review the first edits and settle the caption style.
 Week two
 Send a longer recording with several moments in it. Approve the first batch and use revisions on anything close but not final.
 Week three
 Film around what the first batch showed you worked, then upload it. Ask for a different opening on one video to compare.
 Week four
 Use up the remaining videos with a final batch and start planning next month's shoots. Unused videos do not roll over, so batches are best spread across the weeks.

 Reels are where the UAE's visual businesses already compete
 Walk through any Dubai or Abu Dhabi feed and the pattern is clear: property launches, restaurant openings, beauty clinics, boutiques, hotels and personal brands all use Reels to show a place, a product or a person in under a minute. The ideas are rarely the problem.  20CLIPS is a dedicated Reels editing service. The price is $999 a month in US dollars for 20 videos, roughly $50 per Reel, with 2 revisions on each and no long-term commitment.

 What makes a Reel feel native
 The details separate a Reel from a cropped video.
 Framed around the interface
 Instagram places the account name, caption and buttons over the picture. Faces, key products and captions have to sit clear of those zones, so the edit is composed for 9:16 and not simply cropped from a wide shot.
 The first frame is the hook and the cover
 A Reel is judged before anyone reads a word. It should open on a face, a result or a question instead of a logo animation, and the same frame often becomes what people see on your profile grid.
 Captions in a style you own
 Font, weight, colour and highlight are set once from your references and repeated. Captions that sit under the buttons or look too small on a phone defeat the point.
 Cuts that feel quick and natural
 Reels that feel at home use brisk, purposeful cuts, light zooms and supporting b-roll. Heavy effects tend to look like adverts and get skipped.
 Sound that supports the picture
 Clean voice, a fitting music bed and well-placed effects make the same footage feel polished. Trending audio is chosen and licensed by you, and 20CLIPS can cut to it.
 How a month of Reels works
 The process begins with a 30-minute call about the Reels you want to make, the look you are after and how often you will film. Turnaround and your delivery schedule are agreed there rather than assumed.
 Then you upload clips to the shared folder: talking-head recordings, product shots, behind-the-scenes footage, UGC or podcast sessions. Many UAE accounts upload after each shoot, for example a new menu on Monday and a showroom walk-through on Thursday. Finished Reels come back for review, and each includes 2 revisions for changes to captions, openings or music.
 Approved Reels are final files. You schedule and post them with the rest of your content calendar. If you are weighing whether to outsource the work at all, this guide to outsourcing Reels editing walks through the decision.
 What to film and what to skip
 Vertical footage gives the editor more to work with than a wide shot that has to be reframed. If a venue can only be filmed wide, send it anyway, because the editor can still build a strong Reel from it.
 Raw clips in the highest quality you have, vertical where possible
 Longer sessions that can be cut into several Reels
 Reels from other accounts whose style you want
 Brand fonts, colours and logo
 The point of each Reel, if you have one in mind
 Mistakes that cost a Reel
 Filming horizontally out of habit
 A long greeting before the point
 Captions that are small or sit low
 Changing the look from post to post
 Ignoring the first frame as a cover
 Editing Reels in the app, hiring or subscribing
 Editing inside Instagram is quick for one clip, and limited for captions, b-roll and sound. Doing it twenty times a month usually means it stops. An in-house social editor is strong if Reels are one part of a bigger role, but in the UAE that means salary, visa and equipment for a task that can run as a service.
 Freelancers are fine for a single project; for a steady cadence the briefing starts again each time. A monthly package gives you a fixed fee and the same process every month. The cost page and the hiring guide for the UAE go into detail.

 TikTok rewards how long people watch, and the edit decides that
 On TikTok the feed learns from what people do with a video: whether they stay, rewatch or swipe. That makes editing unusually important. A restaurant in Dubai, a property agent in Abu Dhabi or a founder with a following can film the same clip, and the version with the stronger first second and tighter pacing is the one that keeps people watching.
 20CLIPS edits TikTok videos from the footage you send.  What a good TikTok edit looks like
 Five qualities to look for.
 Retention is the aim of every cut
 Filler is removed, pauses are tightened and the picture keeps changing at the right moments. Each cut gives the viewer a reason to stay for the next beat.
 Hook, build, payoff
 A video that holds attention opens with a hook, builds a clear idea and delivers a payoff before the viewer drifts. Editing finds that structure in raw footage and drops what does not serve it.
 Captions that fit the interface
 TikTok covers the lower part and right edge of the screen. Captions are placed where they can be read, styled to your brand and timed to the voice.
 Sound-on thinking
 TikTok is sound-first more than most platforms. Voice clarity, music and effects shape how native the video feels. Trending audio is left to you for licensing reasons.
 Casual, never careless
 The style is looser than an advert, but still edited. Clean cuts, correct captions and a tidy frame separate intentional from sloppy.
 How the month runs
 The first step is a 30-minute call about the kind of TikTok you make and want more of. Turnaround and your delivery schedule are agreed there.
 After that you upload footage to a shared folder. Talking-head clips, podcast recordings, UGC, screen recordings and b-roll all work, and smaller regular batches are common. A chef might send service footage on Sunday and a founder a recorded Q and A on Wednesday. Videos return for review with 2 revisions each, so a change of hook or caption is quick.
 Finished videos are ready to publish, and posting stays with you. For the thinking behind a good short, read TikTok video editing: what makes a good short .
 Preparing your footage
 Clean voice recording is the cheapest improvement available. A phone held close in a quiet corner beats a better camera in a loud room, and the editor cannot fully fix distorted audio.
 Raw clips, including the parts you think are rough
 Livestream replays and long recordings
 TikToks you want yours to resemble
 Brand fonts, colours and logo
 Any lines or claims that must stay in
 What drags a video down
 A long intro before the point
 Over-editing a casual style
 Posting the same cut everywhere unchanged
 Poor voice recording
 Never reviewing which videos held attention
 Employee, freelancer or monthly package
 Editing in the app is fine for a casual clip and slow for branded output with captions and sound design. A salaried editor is valuable for constant video work, and in the UAE it carries a salary, visa and equipment. A freelancer suits projects, but briefs, quality and price shift from person to person.

 What a good Short does differently
 Five parts of the craft.
 It stands alone
 A good Short is one idea that makes sense without the rest of the video. Context a viewer needs is pulled forward, and anything they do not need is dropped.
 The hook is written by the edit
 In the feed a Short competes with the next one a swipe away. The opening shows the result, the surprising line or the question, and the set-up follows.
 The frame is rebuilt for vertical
 Long-form footage is almost always 16:9. The edit reframes around the speaker or the action so the subject fills the screen, and does not leave a tiny person in the middle of empty bars.
 Captions and graphics carry the point
 Accurate captions, a few emphasised words and simple graphics make a Short readable at a glance and with the sound off.
 It points back to your channel
 A Short works hardest when it makes people curious about the full video. Whether Shorts feed your long-form views or stand alone is a choice you make about the channel, and posting and linking stay with you.
 How a month of Shorts runs
 It starts with a 30-minute call about the channel, the long-form videos you already have and what you want Shorts to do for it. Turnaround and your delivery schedule are agreed there.
 You then share long-form files, a few Shorts whose style you like and your brand fonts and colours. If you know your strongest moments, send timestamps. If not, the editor finds candidates from the recording. Finished Shorts return for review with 2 revisions on each, so a different opening or a trimmed ending is quick to ask for.
 Approved Shorts are ready to upload to your channel. For ideas on volume, read how many short-form videos to post each week .
 What to send, and what to leave out
 Send the whole recording, not a pre-cut highlight. A full session in a Dubai studio or a conference hall offers far more choice than a three-minute teaser.
 The full-length source video or recording in the best quality you have
 Timestamps of moments you already like
 Existing Shorts you want the new ones to resemble
 Your channel's fonts, colours and logo
 Anything that must not be cut, such as a key claim
 Slips to avoid
 Cutting a clip without its set-up
 Leaving a slow opening in
 Keeping the wide framing
 Treating Shorts as leftovers
 Posting once and stopping
 Hire in-house, freelance or subscribe
 Cutting Shorts yourself is realistic for a few and hard for twenty. Reframing, captioning and polishing each one takes much longer than its running time suggests. An in-house video editor makes sense for a channel that publishes long-form all week, and in the UAE that means salary, visa and equipment.
 Freelancers suit a test batch. For a regular channel the repeated briefing and shifting style add up. A monthly package costs $999 for 20 Shorts with 2 revisions each. See what YouTube Shorts editing costs in the UAE and how to hire YouTube Shorts editing in the UAE .

 What UGC editing actually involves
 Five jobs the editor does on every video.
 Keeps it believable and makes it clean
 The edit tidies audio, trims dead air and fixes framing without removing the honesty that makes UGC work.
 Builds hooks that can be tested
 The first seconds decide everything. Editors usually build several openings from one clip, such as a pain point, a result or a question, so you can see which lands. Hook variations are part of the standard service and count within your 20 videos.
 Times the product to the words
 Product shots and overlays land when the creator mentions the thing, so the claim and the proof arrive together.
 Writes in captions for the muted viewer
 Most ad placements start muted. Clear captions and a few on-screen points carry the message.
 Delivers the right formats
 Files are vertical and suit organic posting as well as upload to ad platforms.
 How a month works
 A 30-minute call begins it. You explain the products, the creators and where the videos will run. Turnaround and your delivery schedule are agreed there.
 You then share the brief and references, and upload creator footage to a shared folder as it arrives. Many UAE teams upload creator batches as they land, which spreads the editing across the month.  What makes a clip worth publishing
 Five things the editor looks after.
 A moment that stands alone
 The best clips are a point, a story or a disagreement that makes sense without the episode around it. Finding them means listening to the whole recording, not skimming a transcript.
 A tight cut of real conversation
 Speech has false starts, tangents and long pauses that work in an hour but not in forty seconds. Tightening them while keeping the rhythm of the speaker is the skill that separates a clip from an excerpt.
 Two voices in a vertical frame
 Podcast video is often two or three people at microphones in a wide shot. In a vertical clip the editor cuts between speakers and keeps the active one in view, so it feels like a conversation, not a crop.
 Captions that follow the talk
 Spoken clips depend on captions that are accurate, timed to speech, easy to read and styled to the show.
 A branded look across the show
 A recognisable caption style and palette make clips from the same show feel connected. Your references set it for all 20 videos.
 How a month of clips runs
 A 30-minute call comes first. You describe the show, how many episodes you record and what you want clips to do for it. The delivery schedule is agreed there.
 Then you share the show's logo, fonts, colours and a few clips you like, and upload each episode to a shared folder as it is recorded. Video recordings give the strongest clips, though audio-only shows can use simple visuals and strong captions. Finished clips return for review with 2 revisions each, and you can flag timestamps you want included.
 Approved clips are final files. Posting stays with you. For the method in more depth, read how to turn a podcast into short-form content .
 What to send with each episode
 Record video even if the show is audio-first. Faces make the clips far more engaging, and a camera on each speaker in a Dubai studio costs very little against the extra reach.
 The full episode recording, with video where possible
 Guest names so captions are spelled correctly
 Your show logo, fonts and colours
 Timestamps for moments you already like
 Clips from other shows whose style you admire
 Common slips
 Sending only audio when video exists
 Clipping a punchline without its set-up
 Making clips as long as the topic
 Leaving the guest's name out
 Posting clips only when an episode drops
 Do it yourself, hire a producer or subscribe
 Clipping one or two moments yourself is realistic. Twenty a month on top of recording and publishing the show is not. A producer on the payroll suits a network with a full production team, and in the UAE means salary, visa and equipment. A freelancer per episode is flexible, though each episode needs a new brief and the look can drift.
 A monthly package costs $999 for 20 clips and runs the same way every month. See what podcast clip editing costs in the UAE and how to hire podcast clip editing in the UAE .

 The problem this solves for UK teams
 Almost every UK marketing team has the same bottleneck. Filming is manageable: a product demo in the stockroom, a founder interview, a talk at an industry event, a day of customer visits. Editing is where the work stalls, because turning an hour of footage into a handful of vertical videos with captions, sound and a proper opening takes someone who edits for a living, and most small and mid-sized teams do not have that person.
 20CLIPS is a short-form editing service built around that bottleneck. You send raw material and a few references. An editor finds the strongest moments, restructures them so the point comes first, adds captions, b-roll, music and motion graphics, and returns 9:16 files formatted for Instagram Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts. The price is $999 a month in US dollars for 20 videos, which is about $50 each, and nothing is added per video.
 That makes it easy to plan around. A UK head of marketing can budget a flat figure, an agency can add capacity without recruiting, and a creator can keep posting while filming the next project. The full breakdown of what is included is on the pricing page .

 The craft behind a video people finish
 An opening that earns the next second
 Viewers decide almost immediately. The edit puts the clearest visual or the sharpest line first and removes any warm-up. With a long recording this often means pulling a sentence from the middle to the front.
 Rhythm instead of a fixed pace
 Cuts, zooms and captions land where the idea changes. Talking-head footage in particular needs breaths and false starts removed without making the speaker sound rushed.
 Readable, accurate captions
 Many people watch muted on a commute or in a queue, so captions are the message. They are timed to speech, sized for a phone and placed clear of platform buttons.
 Sound that was mixed
 Voice is levelled, music sits underneath and effects are sparing. A UK brand posting in a crowded feed cannot afford muddy audio.
 One look across the month
 Fonts, colours and caption style are set from your references on day one and repeated across all 20 videos.
 How the monthly process runs
 Start with a 30-minute call. You describe what you make, where it is posted and how often footage will arrive, and you agree turnaround and a delivery schedule that fits your volume. There is nothing to install: the work happens in a shared folder.
 Drop footage in as it is shot. Many UK clients upload after each shoot day instead of saving everything for month end, which spreads the editing and lets you correct style early. Edited videos return for review, and each includes 2 revisions, so feedback on a caption, a hook or a music choice is part of the process.
 Approved videos are finished files. Scheduling and posting stay with you. If you are comparing ways to get this done, this guide to outsourcing editing is a good starting point.
 What to send, and what holds a month back
 Raw files beat polished ones. A full forty-minute interview lets the editor choose what to use, where a three-minute cut limits them.
 Original footage straight from the camera or phone
 Long recordings such as webinars, interviews and talks
 Videos whose style you like, as references
 Brand fonts, colours and logo
 Anything that must be kept in or left out
 Common slips
 Sending only the shortlisted clips, which removes the choice of opening
 Giving notes from several people in separate emails
 A different look each week
 Compressed copies instead of the original files
 Saving every upload for the last days of the month
 Freelancer, in-house or package: the UK view
 Hiring a UK editor in-house means salary, employer costs, equipment, software and someone to manage them. It is a good decision for a business with video every day and a poor one for a business that needs around 20 videos a month. Freelancers are flexible, but every project starts with a new brief and the look shifts between people.
 A package sits in the middle. You pay a fixed amount, get a repeatable process and keep the freedom to leave, since there is no long-term commitment. For the numbers see what short-form editing costs in the UK , and for a checklist see how to hire short-form editing in the UK .

 Five signs of a Reel that was edited properly
 It was composed for the screen
 Instagram draws the username, caption and buttons over the video. A properly edited Reel keeps the face, the product and the captions clear of them.
 The opening does the work
 No logo sting and no 'hi everyone'. The Reel opens on the result, the surprise or the question, and the same first frame doubles as your grid cover.
 The captions look like yours
 Typeface, weight, colour and highlight style are agreed up front and reused, so your Reels read as one account.
 Cuts and movement feel native
 Short, purposeful cuts and gentle zooms feel at home on Instagram. Over-produced effects look like adverts and tend to be skipped.
 The audio was mixed
 Voices are levelled, music sits under them and effects are kept light. You supply any trending audio you want, since licensing is yours.
 The monthly rhythm
 You start with a 30-minute call about your Reels and your look, and the delivery schedule is set there. After that, clips go into the shared folder when they exist.  A back catalogue is a Shorts backlog
 Most UK channels and businesses that record video have the same hidden asset: a back catalogue of long content that gets watched once. Explainer videos, webinars, conference talks, how-to sessions and interviews all contain strong moments that were never pulled out. Shorts are how those moments reach people who would never sit through the full thing.
 20CLIPS turns long recordings into Shorts. You send the video and some references.  What goes into a Short that works
 A moment that stands alone
 The editor looks for an idea that makes sense without the rest of the video. If the viewer needs context, it is brought forward; if they do not, it is dropped.
 A strong first line
 A Short competes with the next one in the feed. The opening presents the result, a surprising sentence or the question, then the set-up.
 A frame designed for portrait
 A 16:9 source is reframed around the speaker or the action and does not simply shrink into a vertical box.
 Captions that carry the idea
 Accurate captions with a few emphasised words let someone follow with the sound off.
 A route back to the channel
 A good Short makes people curious about the rest. What you do with links and descriptions stays with you.
 The monthly process
 A 30-minute call comes first. You describe your channel and your back catalogue, say what you want Shorts to achieve and agree a delivery schedule that fits.
 Then the files go into a shared folder: full videos or recordings, a few Shorts you like and your brand fonts and colours. If you already know the best moments, send timestamps; if not, the editor suggests candidates. Finished Shorts return with 2 revisions each, so a changed opening or a shorter ending is a simple request.
 Approved Shorts are ready for you to upload. To work out how many to post, read how many short-form videos to post each week .
 Sending the right material
 Whole recordings beat highlight reels. A two-hour conference session offers a lot more to choose from than the three minutes someone thought were best.
 The full video or recording at the best quality you have

 What the editor does with a UGC clip
 Cleans without sterilising

 Builds more than one opening

 Lines up the product

 Anatomy of a clip that works
 It needs no context
 A good clip is one idea that makes sense without the rest of the episode, whether a story, an opinion or a quick lesson. The editor listens to the full recording to find them.
 The speech has been tightened
 Conversation contains hesitations and tangents that are fine over an hour and tiresome in forty seconds. Cutting them while keeping the natural rhythm is the difference between a clip and an excerpt.
 The frame suits a phone
 A wide shot of two people at microphones becomes a vertical clip that cuts between them and keeps whoever is speaking in view.
 Captions follow every word
 Spoken clips live or die on captions that are accurate, well timed and easy to read.
 The show feels like one show
 A repeated caption style and palette make clips from different episodes look related.
 The month in practice
 It starts with a 30-minute call about the show: how many episodes you record, who the audience is and what you want clips to achieve. You agree a delivery schedule there.
 You then send your logo, fonts, colours and some clips you admire, and upload each episode to a shared folder after recording. Video gives the best clips, although an audio-only show can use simple visuals with strong captions. Clips return for review with 2 revisions each, and you can mark timestamps you care about.
 Approved clips are finished files that you publish. For a step-by-step view of the approach, read how to turn a podcast into short-form content .
 Sending episodes the helpful way
 If your show is audio-first, consider pointing a camera at the table anyway. The extra reach from clips with faces on them tends to repay the small effort of setting it up.
 The full recording, with video if you have it
 Names of the guests and the show
 Logo, fonts and colours
 Timestamps you already like
 Clips from shows you would like yours to resemble
 Ways clips go wrong
 Audio-only files when video exists
 A punchline with no set-up
 Clips as long as the topic
 No guest name on screen
 Posting clips only on release day

 A host who clips their own show usually manages a couple of moments and then the habit fades. A producer on the payroll makes sense for a publisher with a full team, and means salary, employer costs and equipment. A freelancer per episode can work, but every episode starts from a fresh brief.
 A monthly package keeps the fee and the method constant. For the numbers read what podcast clip editing costs in the UK , and for a checklist read how to hire podcast clip editing in the UK .

 What a well-edited short video has
 Check any finished video against these.
 A first second that gives a reason to stay
 The strongest line or image goes first. Greetings and slow fades are removed, and with long recordings the best moment is often moved to the front.
 Cuts that follow the idea
 The picture changes when the thought changes. Pauses are removed without making the speaker sound hurried.
 Captions that carry the video
 A lot of people watch without sound. Captions are accurate, easy to read at arm's length and kept away from the on-screen buttons.
 Audio that was tidied
 Voice is levelled, music sits under the speech and effects are used with restraint. Wind on a job site and echo in a hall are common problems that a good edit manages.
 Brand consistency
 Fonts, colours and caption style come from your references and repeat across all 20 videos.
 How a month runs
 It starts with a 30-minute call to cover what you film, where you publish and how often you will send footage. Turnaround and your delivery schedule are agreed there, based on your volume, so nobody is working to an assumption.
 Then you upload footage as and when it exists. Many Australian clients send a batch after each shoot instead of waiting for the month to end. Each video comes back for review with 2 revisions included, which means a different opening or a changed caption is a note rather than a new request.
 When a video is approved it is a finished file. Posting stays with you or your team, so you can schedule it with the rest of your content. For a plain-language description of the role, see what a short-form video editor does .
 Sending footage well
 If you can, film vertically and record clean sound. A cheap clip-on microphone helps more than a better camera, because audio problems are the hardest to hide.
 Original footage from the camera or phone
 Longer recordings of talks, sessions and interviews
 A few videos you want yours to feel like
 Brand fonts, colours and logo
 Notes on lines or moments that must stay
 Easy ways to lose time
 Uploading only pre-cut clips so there is no choice of opening
 Passing feedback in pieces from several people
 Redesigning the look mid-month
 Sending files exported from a social app
 Leaving every upload to the last week
 Hire, freelance or subscribe
 An Australian business thinking about editing usually has three options. Hiring someone adds wages, on-costs, equipment and supervision, which is hard to justify for 20 videos a month. A freelancer can be great for a single project but means a fresh brief each time.
 The monthly package is a fixed fee with a repeatable process and no long-term commitment, so it can start small and be dropped if your plans change. The money side is on what short-form editing costs in Australia , and the buying side is on how to hire short-form editing in Australia .

 The difference between a Reel and a cropped clip
 Five things worth checking on any finished Reel.
 It leaves room for Instagram
 The app lays buttons, a caption and your name over the picture. A properly made Reel keeps the face, the product and the text out of those areas.
 The first second is the pitch
 Open on the result or the question. The same frame often becomes your grid cover, so it needs to look good on its own.
 Captions have a style
 One typeface, one colour set, one way of highlighting a key word, repeated across every Reel.
 The cutting feels like Instagram
 Brisk, deliberate cuts and a few light zooms. Heavy effects read as advertising and get scrolled past.
 The sound was handled
 Voice is levelled and any background noise, such as wind outdoors or a coffee machine, is managed. Music is chosen and licensed by you.
 A month, from first call to final file
 It begins with a 30-minute call covering your Reels, your look and how often you will film. You agree turnaround and a delivery schedule there, based on your volume.
 Then you upload clips to a shared folder whenever you have them. It is common for Australian clients to send a batch after each shoot instead of leaving it all until the end.  How to tell a TikTok has been edited properly
 Five checks.
 Each cut earns the next second
 Filler is trimmed, pauses are tightened and the picture refreshes at the right moments.
 There is a shape to it
 Hook, build, payoff. If a recording does not have one, the editor finds it, often by reordering.
 Captions sit in the safe area
 TikTok draws its own interface over the bottom and right of the screen. Captions stay clear of it and follow the speech.
 Audio is intentional
 Clean voice, a fitting music bed and a few effects. Trending sounds are yours to choose and license.
 It feels like TikTok
 Looser than an advert but not careless: accurate captions, clean cuts, a tidy frame.

 The craft in a Short
 What to look for in a finished one.
 It makes sense alone
 A good Short is one idea that needs no other context. The editor pulls forward what the viewer needs and drops what they do not.
 The first line works hard
 The opening shows the result, the surprising sentence or the question, with the set-up following.
 The frame suits a phone
 A wide source is reframed around the speaker or the action, not shrunk into a vertical box.
 Captions do the carrying
 Accurate, readable captions with a few emphasised words work with the sound off.
 It leaves a trail
 A good Short makes people curious about the rest of the channel. Links and descriptions stay with you.
 How a month runs
 A 30-minute call starts it. You describe your channel, say what you want Shorts to do and agree a delivery schedule that suits you.
 You then upload long-form files, some Shorts whose style you like and your brand fonts and colours to a shared folder. Finished Shorts return for review with 2 revisions each, so changing the opening or trimming an ending is simple.

 Keep recording the long version. Even if you think a session was ordinary, a long file gives the editor a lot to choose from, and the best moment is often not the one you expected.

 Five things happen on every video.

 Over-polishing authentic clips
 Only one opening tested
 Forgetting that many viewers watch muted
 Dropping the demonstration
 Sending files without a brief
 Employee, freelancer or monthly service
 Asking creators to edit their own footage leads to uneven quality. An employee brings wages, on-costs, equipment and supervision, which is more than around 20 videos a month usually needs. A freelancer per video suits a campaign but needs briefing each time.
 A monthly service is one fee and one process, with no lock-in. See what UGC editing costs in Australia and how to hire UGC editing in Australia .

 Recorded remotely, clipped remotely
 Plenty of Australian podcasts are made across distances: the host in Sydney, a guest in Perth, an editor somewhere else again. The recording tools already assume nobody is in the same room. Clip editing can work the same way, so the post-production does not need to wait for a person to be in the right city.
 20CLIPS turns each episode into clips for Instagram Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts. The editor listens to the recording, picks the strongest moments, tightens the speech, frames the speakers for portrait and adds captions, pacing and basic motion graphics. The fee is $999 a month, charged in US dollars, for 20 videos at around $50 each. Every clip has 2 revisions and nothing locks you in.
 Everything runs through a shared folder. See the pricing page for the full list of inclusions, and podcast video editing for the wider service.

 What the editor is actually doing
 Five parts of the work.
 Listening for a self-contained moment
 A clip should make sense without the episode around it, so the editor listens through the whole recording instead of searching a transcript.
 Tightening without flattening
 False starts and long pauses go, but the speaker's natural rhythm stays. That is what makes it feel like a clip and not an excerpt.
 Framing the speakers
 Wide shots with two or three people become portrait clips that cut between them and keep the person speaking in view.
 Captioning every word
 Accurate, timed captions that are easy to read on a phone.
 Keeping the look consistent
 One caption style and palette across clips from different episodes.
 How a month goes
 Start with a 30-minute call about the show: how many episodes you record, who listens and what you want clips to do. You agree the delivery schedule there.
 Then share your logo, fonts, colours and a few clips you like, and upload each episode as it is recorded. Video gives the best clips, and audio-only shows can use simple visuals with strong captions. Clips come back for review with 2 revisions each, and you can mark timestamps you want.
 Approved clips are finished files for you to post. For more on the method, read how to turn a podcast into short-form content .
 Tips for sending episodes
 If guests join remotely, ask them to record their own side locally as well. Cleaner audio and picture make better clips, and the editor can use whichever track is stronger.
 The whole recording, with video where possible
 Guest names and the show name
 Logo, fonts and colours
 Timestamps you already like
 Clips from shows you admire
 What weakens clips
 Sending only audio when video exists
 Taking a punchline without its set-up
 Letting clips run as long as the topic
 Leaving off guest names
 Posting clips only on release day
 Do it yourself, hire or subscribe
 Cutting your own clips is fine for a handful, but twenty a month alongside recording and promotion is a lot to ask of a host. A producer on the payroll brings wages, on-costs and equipment, which is more than a clip workload of this size needs. A freelancer per episode can help, though each episode needs a new brief.
 A monthly package is one fee and one method. See what podcast clip editing costs in Australia and how to hire podcast clip editing in Australia .

 Video on a subscription, without the surprises
 Most small Australian businesses do not need a full-time video editor, but they do need video every week.  How a month runs
 You begin with a 30-minute call about what you make and where it is posted. You share reference videos and brand files, and agree how often footage will arrive. Turnaround and your delivery schedule are agreed there, based on your volume.
 Each month then follows the same pattern. You upload footage to a shared folder, edited videos come back for review and you use your 2 revisions per video. Approved videos are finished files for you to publish. Many Australian clients send a batch after each shoot, such as a day on site or a recorded class, which spreads the work across the month.
 Unused videos do not roll over, so sending footage in batches is the habit that matters. To choose a sensible volume, read how many short-form videos to post each week .
 What the package leaves to you
 The package edits what you send. Keeping the scope that tight is what keeps the price flat, and it means you know what a month will and will not include.
 If you think you will need more than 20 videos, say so on the 30-minute call and it will be discussed before you commit.
 Worth knowing before you start
 You write the scripts and plan the content
 You film the footage
 You post and schedule
 You license any specific music
 The standard volume is 20 videos
 Package, freelancer, employee or agency
 Freelancers are flexible, but each project starts with a new brief and the result depends on who is free. Employing an editor brings wages, on-costs, equipment and supervision, which only pays off when video is a daily job well beyond 20 videos a month. An agency retainer often adds strategy and filming, which can be exactly what some businesses need and usually costs more than editing alone.
 The package is a fixed fee, a repeatable method and no lock-in. For the figures see what a monthly editing package costs in Australia , and for a checklist see how to choose a monthly editing package in Australia .
